title: Teacher-distilled continuous proposal with over-fetch and packed reranking
question: Can a cheap continuous proposal retain the full-candidate cosine teacher's relevant persistent-state computation across K=4,8,16 budgets?
hypothesis: A student trained with KL distillation to the full-candidate cosine scorer will retain more teacher-relevant state mass than the existing binary/sign-code proposal, and K=8 or K=16 over-fetch will separate budget limitation from proposal-mechanism limitation.

arms.name: exhaustive_cosine
arms.intervention: cosine-score all 64 persistent states with the fixed width-16 representation

arms.name: distilled_prototype_proposal
arms.intervention: student query-to-prototype KL distillation followed by bounded prototype beam and teacher cosine reranking

decision_rule.condition: report proposal retention, actual target recall, end-to-end success, and total arithmetic separately for K=4,8,16
decision_rule.licenses: diagnostic evidence about the learned proposal funnel on the registered workload
decision_rule.does_not_license: a universal retrieval guarantee or hardware wall-clock speedup

decision_rule.condition: actual target recall and end-to-end success approach the exhaustive cosine reference while total arithmetic remains materially lower
decision_rule.licenses: bounded support for a distilled sparse funnel on this workload
decision_rule.does_not_license: broad C5 or general semantic memory claims

held_constant: 48 training semantic codes versus held-out evaluation query codes
distillation state supervision restricted to states whose values are training codes
no evaluation target or address enters distillation
runtime teacher reranking uses only the bounded shortlist
exhaustive reference retrieval scores the complete 64-state population
arithmetic and packing are reported separately from wall-clock behavior
